response.cue_rationale: “Older sister” is a precise sense covered by both answers; Malaysian “kakak” can specifically refer to an older sister in kinship context.

preference_risk.rationale: “Kakak” is plausibly ordinary in both varieties, but its gender specificity differs by language and context.

response.rationale: Both forms can mean an older sister. Indonesian commonly specifies gender with “kakak perempuan,” while Malaysian “kakak” conventionally identifies an older sister in sibling terms, though Indonesian also uses “kakak” more broadly.
response.risk_rationale: “Kakak” may be interpreted as an older sibling of unspecified gender in Indonesian outside context.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Kakak” is also ordinary in Indonesian, but it is broader there; “kakak perempuan” remains a useful Indonesian specification contrasted with Malaysian unmarked “kakak.”
